entry.content: ... that more than one hundred million stars are visible in Zooming In on the Andromeda Galaxy (pictured)?

entry.title: I Hotel (Wikipedia — did you know?)
entry.content: ... that Karen Tei Yamashita realized the structure of her novel, I Hotel, by cutting, folding, and writing on ten cardboard cubes, each representing a year in the book?

entry.title: Carrlyn Bathe (Wikipedia — did you know?)
entry.content: ... that Carrlyn Bathe met her husband after he sent her gear from his clothing brand?

entry.title: near-miss effect (Wikipedia — did you know?)
entry.content: ... that due to the near-miss effect, gamblers may mistake a game of luck for a game of skill?

entry.title: Chauncey Archiquette (Wikipedia — did you know?)
entry.content: ... that tacklers "bounced off" Chauncey Archiquette "as if he were a brick wall"?

entry.title: Timeless Voyage (Wikipedia — did you know?)
entry.content: ... that the author of the comic book Timeless Voyage was the leader of a UFO religion?

entry.title: James Smart (Wikipedia — did you know?)
entry.content: ... that Chief Constable James Smart flooded police courts with over 17,000 cases to prove how impractical it was for home owners to light their own stairs?

entry.title: The Silver Veil and the Golden Gate (Wikipedia — did you know?)
entry.content: ... that an Indiana university argued in court that The Silver Veil and the Golden Gate, a 1914 painting, was too modern for their art collection in 2024?

entry.title: Piri Reis (Wikipedia — did you know?)
entry.content: ... that Piri Reis did not map Antarctica in the sixteenth century?
